scenes.headline: How nac keeps its orchestrator's context a plan
scenes.sub: Arcee's open-source Rust harness: threads, episodes, and workers that vanish.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Acorn! nac is Arcee's open-source agent harness, in Rust. Its orchestrator isn't allowed to touch anything. Here's how.

scenes.label: The split
scenes.text: Keep the temporary context needed to perform an action apart from the persistent state needed to continue a workstream.
scenes.say: The idea: the context an action needs is temporary. The state a workstream needs is persistent. Keep them apart, and take that literally.

steps.say: The orchestrator plans what happens next. Its only action is launching threads; it can't run commands or edit files.
Each dispatch starts a worker: a fresh process and context, given the action, its tools, and the thread's episodes.
The worker uses tools and changes the environment, until the model answers with no tool calls.
That answer is the episode: a handoff, so there's no separate summary. It joins the thread.
Then the worker's context is discarded for good. The world keeps its changes. The record keeps the episode.

items.say: It ends each turn with a batch of thread calls: a target, an action, and optional sources.
A source in the same batch becomes a dependency edge. A finished one just lends its latest episode.
nac rejects cycles and duplicate targets, then runs independent workers at once.
It waits for the whole batch, so the orchestrator never sees a half-finished world.

scenes.quote: a returned error means the environment may have moved ahead of persistent history.
scenes.say: Arcee prints its one seam. Episodes persist only on success, file changes persist anyway, so a dying worker leaves the world ahead of the record.

scenes.text: The orchestrator cannot act, so its context stays a plan. Nothing piles up, so nothing needs compacting.
scenes.say: The orchestrator can't act, so its context stays a plan. Nothing piles up to compact.

recap: Workers act, leave an episode, and vanish
A batch is a graph, run in parallel
scenes.say: To recap: an orchestrator that only dispatches, workers that leave an episode and vanish, and batches run as graphs.
